hlr.text: The tool chain shall not produce object code whose behaviour differs from the semantics of its source without that being detected before the code is used.
No contract shall be reported as proven unless it holds; a contract that is not proven shall stay checked at run time or stop the build (fail-closed).
Isolation properties stated in the source shall be enforced at compile time: pure code performs no I/O, secret data does not steer control flow, foreign data enters as unverified.
Generated programs shall be memory safe: no use of a moved or freed value, and heap integrity independent of when the collector runs.
Every failure of a generated program (arithmetic overflow, division by zero, contract violation, resource exhaustion, exceeded cycle budget) shall be a diagnosed stop, never a silent wrong value.
The tool chain shall be reproducible from its sources and free of influence from an unreviewed binary: self-compilation reaches a bit-identical fixpoint and a diverse double compilation agrees.

A critical output shall be released only when two dissimilar computation channels agree exactly, inside a cycle budget, under a valid translation certificate; any other outcome latches the safe state.
Every certified kernel shall be proven against its contract, translation-validated, covered to decision and MC/DC level by tests that ran on the real binary, and traceable to these requirements.

Object code shall be traceable to its source lines, and every proof, cache and qualification record shall be bound to the exact artifacts it was produced from: a stale, altered, forged or unsigned record is rejected.

The verification tools shall compose into one chain that is reachable through one driver: each tool consumes the artifact the previous one produced, bound to it by hash, and a corruption of any artifact is refused by the tool that consumes it.

llr.title: The lexer accepts the token grammar and stops on a malformed token with a diagnostic and no output.
The parser builds the AST of well-formed programs and stops on a syntax error with a located diagnostic and no output.
The type checker rejects ill-typed programs before code generation.
Contracts are fail-closed: a refuted requires/ensures stops the build with [V0001]; an undecided one stays as a run-time check that traps.
A function declared `/ pure` that reaches an I/O primitive is rejected with [E0200].
A branch whose condition depends on a `@secret` value is rejected with [C0009].
Ownership is linear: a value moved with `own` cannot be used again ([O0001]).
The collector does not change program results however often it runs, and heap exhaustion is a diagnosed stop.
The QF_LIA decision procedure reports `proven` only for valid linear contracts and refutes invalid ones with a counterexample.
The QF_NIA extension reports `proven` only for valid non-linear contracts.
The certificate kernel re-derives every proven obligation independently of the compiler and rejects a tampered certificate.
The translation validator accepts a function only when its x86-64 code has the trap behaviour, value, effects and frame discipline of its AST, and rejects every other code.
The assembler encodes every accepted instruction as GNU as does and rejects what it does not know with [L0001].
A foreign declaration is bound only when its ABI is supported; results enter as `unverified`; anything else is refused with [I0003].
Integer overflow and division by zero stop the program with a diagnostic and a non-zero status.
A function whose structural cycle cost exceeds its `@bound` is rejected with [V0002].
The compiler compiled by itself is bit-identical to the compiler that compiled it, the frozen seed matches its recorded hashes, and the seed-built and self-built compilers agree.
The lockstep voter commits a value only when the x86-64 channel and the LumePuter RV32IM monitor agree inside the cycle budget under a valid certificate; every other case latches SAFE_STATE_TRIP.

The coverage analyzer reports an obligation as covered only with a witness the real binary confirms, and reports unreachable outcomes instead of hiding them: every decision is an obligation, nested ones included; an outcome without a witness is classified only as the false conclusion of a declared law or as infeasible with a kernel proof, and is uncovered otherwise; a certified module with an uncovered obligation fails the qualification.
Every domain kernel of the certified modules is proven against its contract (no obligation left runtime-checked or refuted) and translation-validated.
The traceability checker accepts a requirement only with a parent, a source file, a positive test, a negative test and a mutation gate or proof, and rejects an orphaned matrix.

The translation validator rejects a `@secret` function when its emitted code, or the code of any routine it reaches by call or jmp (user function or runtime helper), holds a conditional branch, a division or a memory access outside its frame ([C0010]).

With `--dwarf` the compiler and the assembler emit DWARF v4 line and symbol information that maps code addresses to source lines; a line directive that names an undeclared file is rejected with [L0001].

The incremental proof cache answers `hit` for a function only when its body, contracts, callee interfaces and prover version digest to a stored record whose seal verifies; a tampered record is refused with [PC0002] and a module the prover refutes is never stored ([PC0003]).
A value sent through a linear channel cannot be used again ([E0305]); a lock acquisition that breaks the rank order or closes a wait-for cycle is rejected ([E0306]); both before code generation.

A `@no_alloc` function is accepted only when it and every function it calls can reach no heap allocation: scalar typed parameters with proven bounds, arithmetic proven inside the immediate range, no heap value, recursion in tail position only ([E0210] otherwise).

With `--check-source` the certificate kernel reads the contracts of the source itself and accepts a certificate only when its hash is that file's and every obligation is, term for term, an obligation of that file; anything it cannot bind is a refusal ([K0010]..[K0017]).

The cryptographic primitives that seal and sign evidence (SHA-256, HMAC, HKDF, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Ed25519, X25519, the TLS 1.3 key schedule, record layer and handshake) reproduce the official vectors and reject every forged tag, signature, record and handshake message.

A kernel is lowered to AArch64, RV64 or RV32 only after the lumec front end accepted it ([T0902] otherwise) and only inside the integer kernel fragment ([T0901] otherwise); the emitted words are translation-validated and behave like the x86-64 code.

A neural cartridge is produced only for the monitor fragment, and its forward pass is accepted only when the tensor hash and the ballast guard hold and the result equals the native and the LumePuter results.
The evidence file is hash-chained section by section and carries a detached Ed25519 signature over its SHA-256 and its chain head; the signature does not verify for an altered section.

Channel B of the envelope is produced by a clean-room front end and code generator whose tool links no compiler module; a defect modelled in the front end or the code generator of ONE channel (a source mutant compiled by that channel only, a corrupted instruction of channel B) latches SAFE_STATE_TRIP.

The split bundle (channel programs and manifest) records the SHA-256 of every artifact; split-verify refuses a bundle whose artifact or manifest hash differs, and a voted request commits only on agreeing, fresh, well-formed frames.

The worst-case stack depth of a `@no_alloc` function is computed in bytes on the emitted text over every path that remains under the proven ranges; text without a bound (a call cycle that is not a tail jump) is rejected.
A run-time check kept by --keep-proven-checks / --critical is code of the function: a kept check that calls a function that is not `@no_alloc` is rejected with [E0210].
The emitted machine code of every integer runtime helper is verified against its specification for all inputs of the modelled cases; a helper whose code differs from the specification is rejected.

Every SMT-LIB certificate the translation validator exports is checked by a native decision procedure that shares no code with it; a certificate that is not the stated claim, or whose claim is not refuted, is not accepted.

A function that is both `@secret` and `@no_alloc` is lowered to straight-line code over immediate integers: a conditional, a call of a function that is not such a kernel, or an operation without a proven range is a compile error ([C0011] / [E0210]); the validator re-derives the ranges and applies [C0010] to every routine the kernel reaches.

X.509 v3 path validation for Ed25519 chains accepts a path only when every signature, validity period, CA constraint and the pinned trust anchor hold, and returns no key otherwise; random bytes and generated keys are released only when the OS entropy health check finds no dead, stuck or repeating source.
The wrapping SIMD lane intrinsics are modelled as 4 * (a + b) only when the lane range is entailed; without it a contract over them is not reported proven and stays a run-time check that traps.

The key that signs the evidence is certified by a self-signed X.509 v3 certificate written with the package; `@verify` accepts a package only when that certificate validates as its own trust anchor and certifies the signing key; a new signing key is generated only when the OS entropy health check passes.

The certificate, the source binding, the object code and its translation validation name one source and one assembly by SHA-256; along the whole chain (proof cache, certificate, assembly, SMT-LIB certificates, runtime helpers, stack bound, coverage, envelope, split bundle, cartridge, signed manifest) a corrupted artifact is refused by the tool that consumes it.
Every step of the chain is a command of one driver whose help, manuals and dispatch table cannot drift apart; an unknown command is an error.

The proof service runs the passes of the compiler in process: it answers with the diagnostic of the compiler for an invalid program instead of aborting, and none of its modes adds a term of higher degree to the run time of the compiler alone.
